book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: Slowly houses start to acquire conservatory?

indicators.note: the word for slowly holds the next piece inside it, as a house holds its occupant

parts.note: lento is the musical direction for a slow tempo

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word acquire is wanted

parts.note: its starting letter is the one used

explanation.surface: Someone is gradually saving up to add a conservatory to the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: a conservatory is one kind of lean-to.
explanation.definitionFit: A lean-to is a structure built against a house wall, and a glazed conservatory is often built that way.

clue.text: African city university occupies country area

indicators.note: the university letter takes up a place inside the country-and-area letters

parts.note: land means a country

explanation.surface: A university campus takes over a stretch of rural land.
explanation.definitionFit: Luanda is the capital of Angola, on Africa's Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Canada geese oddly cold, deserted, missing Mediterranean clime

indicators.note: the letters left of Canada geese are put together in an odd way
the cold and deserted letters are left out of the words Canada geese

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be thinned out and mixed
D is the abbreviation for deserted in cricket and military records

explanation.surface: Wild geese from Canada end up, oddly, in a warm southern climate.
explanation.walkthrough: Oddly looks like a call for odd letters; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aegean Sea is the arm of the Mediterranean between Greece and Turkey, a sunny region.

clue.text: Pipe top of range air-conditioning in the front of Audi

indicators.note: the range and air-conditioning letters go inside the word the

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first letter of range

parts.note: its top, or first letter, is used

indicators.note: the front of a car is where it begins, so the beginning letter of Audi

parts.note: the car make, whose first letter is used

explanation.surface: A top-of-the-range car with air-conditioning piped in at the front of the Audi.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea is the windpipe, the tube carrying air to the lungs.

clue.text: Instrument having new function in shipping forecast area

indicators.note: the new party letters sit inside the sea-area name

parts.note: Malin is one of the sea areas named in the BBC Shipping Forecast, off north-west Ireland
a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: A musician's gear is somehow given a new role in a sea area of the radio forecast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shipping Forecast is the BBC radio bulletin of weather for the sea areas around Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The mandolin is a plucked string instrument with a rounded body and paired strings.

clue.text: Constellation eclipses one which is similar to Mars

indicators.note: the I of the constellation is hidden from view, as an eclipse hides a body

parts.note: Aries, the Ram, is a constellation of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A constellation passes in front of something that resembles the planet Mars.
explanation.walkthrough: Mars here is the Roman god of war, not the planet; his Greek counterpart is the similar figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares was the Greek god of war, the counterpart of the Roman god Mars.

clue.text: Obedient dog initially playing out with Sue

indicators.note: just the first letter of dog

parts.note: its first letter is the one used

indicators.note: the letters of out and Sue are played around with

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A well-trained dog goes out to play with its owner Sue.
explanation.definitionFit: Duteous is an old word for dutiful, doing what one is told.

clue.text: Film actress learning lines, halfway through

parts.note: lore is a body of learning

indicators.note: the letter at the very centre of lines

parts.note: a five-letter word, so its middle letter is the third

explanation.surface: An actress is halfway through learning her lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophia Loren is the Italian star of films such as Two Women.

clue.text: Rock band (anagram)

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Manchester group formed from Joy Division
second meaning: an anagram is the letters put in a ...

explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed word looks like an instruction to rearrange; it is the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: New Order is a famous English group, and an anagram is literally a new order of letters.

clue.text: Hound needing a good hour in presence of blower

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: read literally, the good-hour letters go in the presence of, that is inside, the blower

parts.note: a fan blows air

explanation.surface: A dog wants a good hour beside someone blowing a horn or whistle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Afghan is a breed of sight hound with a long silky coat.

clue.text: Base for take-off/landing damaged earth within to what extent?

indicators.note: the reworked earth goes inside the question word

parts.note: how? asks to what extent

indicators.note: the letters of earth are broken up and reset

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be damaged

explanation.surface: A question about how badly the ground was damaged at an airfield.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathrow is London's main airport, a base where aircraft take off and land.

clue.text: Confectionery favourite obtained from bananas

indicators.note: the favourite has gained the crazed letters inside it

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

indicators.note: slang for crazy, so the letters of from go mad

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone's favourite sweet is made from bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: A pomfret, or Pontefract cake, is a small round liquorice sweet from Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomfret cakes are liquorice sweets, a traditional item of British confectionery.

clue.text: Passing argument somewhere in US prison

parts.note: passing is a euphemism for death
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A passing argument breaks out somewhere inside an American jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Death row is the block in a US prison where inmates sentenced to execution are held.

clue.text: Medical examiner forgets oxygen — an embarrassing position

indicators.note: the examiner leaves out the oxygen symbol

parts.note: a coroner investigates sudden deaths

explanation.surface: A doctor forgetting the oxygen would find themselves in an awkward spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a corner is to be in a difficult situation with no easy way out.

clue.text: In theatre, a cleaner displays over-sentimentality

indicators.note: the answer is sitting inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the run of words the answer is concealed in, across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A cleaner at the theatre shows a sentimental streak.
explanation.definitionFit: Treacle is used figuratively for cloying, excessive sentiment, sweet and sticky like the syrup.

clue.text: Men with rods arranged welcome on region where Trent originates

parts.note: staff are the people employed somewhere

indicators.note: the letters of rods are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be arranged
hi is a greeting
re means on or about

explanation.surface: Anglers with their rods are greeted at the river's source.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Trent rises in Staffordshire, an English county in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Staffordshire is the English county in which the River Trent has its source, on Biddulph Moor.

clue.text: Short trailer, broadcast about book, shown after international

indicators.note: everything else is placed after the letter for international
the reworked letters go round the book letter
scattered like seed, so the letters of trailer are spread anew

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be scattered

explanation.surface: A brief trailer for a book is shown after an international match.
explanation.walkthrough: Short looks like an adjective for trailer, but it is the definition in the sense of short-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: Being short with someone means being curt and bad-tempered, which is irritable.

clue.text: One composed fancy crest, maintaining focal point

indicators.note: the rearranged letters keep the central word inside them
the letters of crest are rearranged fancifully

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be rearranged
a hub is a centre of activity

explanation.surface: Someone composed has designed an elaborate crest with a central point.
explanation.walkthrough: Composed suggests calm; here it means wrote music.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Schubert was the Austrian composer of the Unfinished Symphony and many songs.

clue.text: Reportedly, anorak stalked tea lounge for jazz player

indicators.note: the coat follows behind the other two pieces, as a stalker follows

parts.note: char is British slang for tea
to lie about is to lounge

indicators.note: spoken out loud, the coat word gives the surname

parts.note: a parka is a hooded anorak

explanation.surface: An oddball in an anorak follows someone through a tea room to hear a jazz musician.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, parka is close to the surname; anorak is also British slang for an obsessive, which feeds the stalking picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Parker was the American alto saxophonist who helped create bebop.

clue.text: Attract fish to boost Caribbean islands

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting the letters reads them from the bottom up

parts.note: to draw is to attract
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A plan to attract fish and boost the economy of some Caribbean islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leeward Islands are a chain in the eastern Caribbean, so the word names that group.

clue.text: Funny man gets Japanese fencing delivered when vacating

parts.note: kendo is the Japanese martial art of fencing with bamboo swords

indicators.note: the word delivered emptied of its inside, leaving only its ends

parts.note: with its inside vacated, only its first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: A comedian takes up Japanese sword fighting, which is delivered to him on moving out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken Dodd was a famous English comedian from Liverpool, known for his tickling stick.

clue.text: In hovel, there's no time to be toffee-nosed

indicators.note: the no-time letters go inside the hovel word

parts.note: a sty is a filthy dwelling
taken as written

explanation.surface: Living in a hovel leaves no time for being snobbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee-nosed is British slang for stuck-up, and snotty means the same arrogance.

clue.text: Obscure couples regularly found in county museum events

indicators.note: pairs of letters picked at even six-letter intervals, which here are the central pair of each six-letter word

parts.note: its central pair of letters
its central pair of letters
its central pair of letters

explanation.surface: Obscure couples keep turning up at museum events around the county.
explanation.walkthrough: Each of the three words has six letters, so taking the central two of each is the same as taking a couple every sixth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unseen is hidden from view, which is one meaning of obscure.

clue.text: European to take the plunge in Serpentine's perimeter

indicators.note: the marrying word goes inside the outer letters
the outside letters of Serpentine

parts.note: the lake's name, its outside letters being its perimeter
colloquially, to get married

explanation.surface: A European tourist dives into the Serpentine near its edge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Serpentine is the lake in London's Hyde Park; taking the plunge looks like a swim but means marrying.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swede is a native of Sweden, a European country.

clue.text: Marine life scheme working on banks of Kennet

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another is placed after it

parts.note: a plan is a scheme

indicators.note: the banks of a river are its edges, so only the outside letters of Kennet

parts.note: the river name, whose ends are used
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: A conservation scheme for river life is underway beside the Kennet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kennet is a river in southern England; its banks are its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plankton is the mass of tiny drifting organisms that live in the sea.

clue.text: River smell addressed

indicators.note: as in a spoken address, the smell word is said out loud

parts.note: an odour is a smell

explanation.surface: Someone complains about the smell coming from the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a major European river forming much of the border between Germany and Poland.

clue.text: Babe close to three years grasps dance moves

indicators.note: the end letter of the word three

parts.note: its closing letter is the one used

indicators.note: the year letters hold the reworked dance between them

parts.note: y is the abbreviation for year, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: the letters of dance are moved around

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be moved

explanation.surface: A toddler of nearly three grabs at some dance steps.
explanation.walkthrough: Babe looks like a baby, given the three years; it is slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye candy is slang for someone visually attractive, as is babe.

clue.text: Gold filling … best to decline sweet

indicators.note: gold goes inside the other piece
the letters of best are bent out of their order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be reordered
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A gold filling means it is best to refuse a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: The dentist picture makes decline mean refuse; here it is the signal to rearrange best.
explanation.definitionFit: A sorbet is a water ice served as a dessert, which Britons call a sweet.

clue.text: Man ripped clothes working hoe, ending in shed

indicators.note: used as a verb: the ripped word dresses the rest

parts.note: tore means ripped

indicators.note: the letters of hoe are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be worked

indicators.note: only the last letter of shed

parts.note: its final letter is the one used

explanation.surface: A man tore his clothes hoeing the garden and ended up in the shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Theodore is a man's first name, and a name is a common crossword way of giving a man.

clue.text: Jockey comparatively embarrassed losing first Yankee

indicators.note: the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red, so more embarrassed is redder
Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A rider looks more sheepish after losing to an American in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat Eddery was a champion flat-racing jockey in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddery is the surname of Pat Eddery, many times British champion jockey.
